title: Traffic Lifecycle Manager for Versioned Model Experiments
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Goal: Build a Traffic Lifecycle Manager (TLM) that orchestrates safe A/B and canary rollouts for model versions by controlling per-request exposure, running shadow probes, and executing statistically principled auto-rollback actions. The TLM will be the policy and enforcement layer integrated with the Console, routing plane, and runtime. It should let PM/Engineers define experiments in a concise DSL (traffic schedules, cohorts, stop conditions), apply sampling bias correction, and produce deterministic exposure for reproducible analysis.

Key capabilities: traffic schedules and gradual ramps, cohort scoping (user segments, geos, API keys), shadow mirroring with selective payload sampling, per-cohort sequential hypothesis tests with configurable alpha/beta, power-based minimum sample enforcement, adaptive early-stop rules, automated rollback triggers (metric delta thresholds + drift indicators), and audit trails for compliance. The system must integrate with existing observability (token-level cost, latency, quality signals) and emit structured events for the Console to show experiment health and suggested actions.

Design constraints: enforce low-latency SLOs (canary exposure must not increase tail latency beyond configured budget), provide deterministic seeding for traffic assignment to avoid allocation churn, support both hosted and Dedicated/Private deployments via policy sync, and allow safety overrides (manual pause/revert) for enterprise customers.

Trade-offs discussed: we prioritize strong statistical guarantees and reproducibility over ultra-fine-grained split control; this means experiments are slightly heavier to configure upfront but safer in production. Shadow traffic sampling will be limited (configurable) to control cost. Auto-rollback is conservative by default (requires both primary metric breach and drift on secondary metrics) to avoid oscillations.
acceptance_criteria:
1) Experiment DSL implemented and validated in staging: traffic schedule, cohort selector, stop rules.
2) Per-request deterministic assignment reproducible across restarts (seed documented).
3) Sequential statistical checks compute p-values and confidence intervals in the runtime pipeline and surface results to Console.
4) Shadow mirroring works end-to-end for a sampled subset without exceeding latency SLOs.
5) Auto-rollback executes when configured trigger conditions are met; Console records rollback reason and implicated metrics.
6) End-to-end integration tests with simulated traffic and synthetic degradations (latency/quality) exist and pass.
7) Runbook for manual override and incident response is published in Confluence.
tasks: Product: Finalize DSL syntax and guardrail defaults; produce short PRD and examples.
Design: Wireframes for Console experiment canvas (setup, live health, rollback modal).
Eng (Runtime): Implement deterministic traffic assignment and low-latency shadow path.
Eng (Analytics): Implement sequential testing library with power calculations and false-positive controls.
Eng (Routing): Add enforcement hooks to routing layer to apply exposure percentages and cohort filters.
SRE: Cost guard to cap shadow sampling and auto-throttle if infra pressure detected.
QA: Create synthetic traffic harness and failure injection scenarios for canary and revert behavior.
Docs: Quickstart, examples (canary, A/B, shadow) and runbook for rollback/override.
Security: Review audit trail events for PII and KMS/HSM compatibility for Private deployments.
updates: 2026-02-12: Kickoff with Eng, Design, Analytics; agreed on DSL first pass and minimum viable controls.
2026-02-18: Analytics spike completed — sequential testing approach chosen (alpha spending + early stop) to reduce false positives in short canaries.
2026-02-24: Design studio: Console canvas draft reviewed; required quick actions (pause/revert) added to top-right toolbar per PM feedback.
2026-02-27: Trade-off decision: default auto-rollback requires both primary metric breach and a correlated secondary metric drift to avoid noisy reverts. Marked in PRD.
2026-03-01: Assigned initial eng tasks; runtime implementation scoped to include deterministic hashing and a shadow sampler capped at 5% by default.
Next steps: Allocate 2 sprints for runtime+analytics, 1 sprint for Console integration, schedule security review in Cycle 2026-W11.
notes: Metric selection guidance: primary metric should be customer-facing (quality or conversion); secondary metrics: latency, error rate, cost-per-token.
Consider adding a synthetic probe job that periodically injects labelled requests to detect silent regressions in quality signals not exposed by production traffic.
Ensure experiment events include model version, variant id, cohort id, assignment seed, and sampling rate for full auditability.
Plan for a feature flag to disable auto-rollback at org level for enterprise customers who prefer manual governance.
Monitoring: emit anomaly score and N-day drift signal; tie automatic rollback to both absolute delta and anomaly persistence window.
